catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 pediatric data at PES
detailed_catalyst_text: New clinical data were presented showing efficacy of therapy in pediatric acquired hypothalamic obesity, including 2.5‑year durability from a Phase 2 extension and one‑year outcomes from the Phase 3 TRANSCEND pediatric subgroup. Results showed sustained reductions in multiple weight measures and meaningful improvements in weight categories versus placebo. These findings support durable benefit and safety in a high‑need pediatric population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ashley Shoemaker, M.D., MSCI, Associate Professor of Pediatrics, Pediatric Endocrinology at Vanderbilt Health, presented a poster on 2026-05-01 with data on the continued efficacy and safety after 2.5 years of setmelanotide treatment in pediatric patients following their participation in the 16-week Phase 2 trial. Pediatric patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity who received setmelanotide for up to 2.5 years achieved sustained reductions across multiple age‑adjusted weight‑related measures. Jennifer Miller, M.D., Professor of Pediatrics, Pediatric Endocrinology, University of Florida College of Medicine, presented data from the Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial in an oral presentation on 2026-05-02 on the changes in weight category in the pediatric subpopulation of participants after 1 year of setmelanotide treatment. After 1 year of treatment, 71.1% of pediatric patients treated with setmelanotide (n=32) improved by ≥1 weight category, and 44.4% (n=20) improved by ≥2 weight categories, compared with 13.6% (n=3) improving one weight category and 0% improving two categories for placebo patients.

catalyst_text: Received EU authorization and US approval for indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The European Commission expanded the marketing authorization to include treatment of obesity and control of hunger in adults and children 4 years and older with acquired hypothalamic obesity due to hypothalamic injury or impairment. The U.S. FDA previously approved a supplemental NDA on 2026-03-19 for the same indication. These approvals make the first therapy available for this rare condition and support wider patient access across both regions.
catalyst_text_evidence: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. today announced the European Commission (EC) has expanded the marketing authorization for IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) to include the treatment of obesity and control of hunger in adults and children 4 years of age and above with acquired hypothalamic obesity (HO) due to hypothalamic injury or impairment. The Company's supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on 2026-03-19 for IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) to treat patients in the United States living with acquired HO.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval and positive CHMP opinion
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported that CHMP adopted a positive opinion to expand the EU marketing authorization to include adults and children 4 years and older with acquired hypothalamic obesity due to hypothalamic injury or impairment. The announcement also referenced that the FDA approved the same indication in the United States the prior week. This reflects meaningful regulatory progress for this rare neuroendocrine condition.
catalyst_text_evidence: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ... announced that the European Medicines Agency's (EMA) Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) has adopted a positive opinion recommending to expand the current marketing authorization for IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) to include the treatment of obesity and the control of hunger in adults and children 4 years of age and above with acquired hypothalamic obesity (HO) due to hypothalamic injury or impairment. "The positive CHMP opinion with a broad label following closely upon last week's FDA approval validates the quality of the data which supports our filings in acquired HO and further confirms our global approach to drug development," said David Meeker, M.D. In the United States, setmelanotide is indicated to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults and pediatric patients aged 4 years and older with acquired hypothalamic obesity, in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older with syndromic or monogenic obesity due to Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) or Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC), proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 1 (PCSK1), or leptin receptor (LEPR) deficiency confirmed by genetic testing demonstrating variants in POMC, PCSK1, or LEPR genes that are interpreted as pathogenic, likely pathogenic, or of uncertain significance (VUS).

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for expanded obesity indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved an expanded indication for setmelanotide to treat acquired hypothalamic obesity in adults and pediatric patients aged 4 years and older. This represents the first and only approved therapy for this condition, addressing a significant unmet medical need.
catalyst_text_evidence: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:RYTM), a global commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on transforming the lives of patients living with rare neuroendocrine diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved an expanded indication for IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) to treat patients living with acquired hypothalamic obesity (HO). With this label expansion, IMCIVREE is indicated to reduce excess body weight and maintain reduction long term in adults and pediatric patients aged 4 years and older with acquired HO. IMCIVREE is now the first and only FDA-approved therapy for acquired HO, offering a targeted approach that addresses the underlying biology of this disease and meets a critical unmet need for patients who previously had no treatment options.

catalyst_text: Announced negative topline results from Phase 3 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from the EMANATE Phase 3 trial reported that four genetic substudies did not meet the prespecified primary endpoint of placebo-adjusted BMI change at Week 52 in patients with MC4R pathway–related obesity due to heterozygous variants in POMC/PCSK1, LEPR, SRC1, or SH2B1. Post hoc analyses showed statistically significant BMI reductions in the POMC/PCSK1 and SRC1 substudies among modified ITT and completer populations, highlighting potential benefit in targeted subgroups.
catalyst_text_evidence: BOSTON, 2026-03-16 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:RYTM) ... today announced the topline results from its EMANATE trial. The four substudies of this global, Phase 3 trial evaluating setmelanotide did not meet primary endpoints. The primary endpoint was the difference in mean percent change in BMI from baseline to Week 52 versus placebo, analyzed in the modified intent-to-treat (ITT) population using prespecified multiple imputation to account for missing values and discontinuations. Topline results include: POMC / PCSK1 Hets (N=78): –4.3% placebo-adjusted reduction in BMI (p=0.15); LEPR Hets (N=23): –3.6% placebo-adjusted reduction in BMI (p=0.94); SRC1 (NCOA1) (N=73): –4.0% placebo-adjusted reduction in BMI (p=0.12); and SH2B1 (N=121): –1.7% placebo-adjusted reduction in BMI (p=0.43). According to post hoc analyses based on last observation carried forward (LOCF) for missing values, setmelanotide achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful BMI reductions at Week 52 in the modified intent-to-treat patient populations in the POMC/PCSK1 Hets and SRC1 substudies: –5.5% least-squares mean difference in BMI in POMC/PCSK1 Hets patients (n=78; p=0.0010); and –6.2% least-squares mean difference in BMI in SRC1 (NCOA1) patients (n=73; p<0.0001).

detailed_catalyst_text: Reported additional positive 52-week results from the Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity, expanding the dataset to 142 patients including a Japanese cohort and supplemental patients. Outcomes showed a -18.8% placebo-adjusted BMI reduction and significant hunger score improvements. The supplemental NDA for this indication is under FDA review with a PDUFA goal date, underscoring regulatory momentum supported by robust efficacy data.
catalyst_text_evidence: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ... today announced additional positive data from its global Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial of setmelanotide in patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity (HO). Highlights from these 52-week data include: -18.8% placebo-adjusted difference1 in BMI reduction (N=142); Primary endpoint of mean BMI reduction of -16.4% from baseline for all patients on setmelanotide therapy (n=94) compared with +2.4% BMI change for patients on placebo (n=48) at 52 weeks (95% CI; p<0.0001); and Among patients aged 12 and older (n=98), the setmelanotide group (n=66) showed an average weekly reduction of 2.5 points in the weekly average most hunger score, compared with a 1.3‑point reduction in the placebo group (n=32) (p=0.0015). The Company's supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) is under review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) with a PDUFA goal date of 2026-03-20.

catalyst_text: Reported positive interim Phase 2 data in PWS
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary results from an exploratory Phase 2 study in Prader-Willi syndrome showed reductions in BMI and hyperphagia at Months 3 and 6. Seventeen of eighteen patients remained on treatment and safety was consistent with the established profile, indicating potential therapeutic benefit.
catalyst_text_evidence: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:RYTM) ... today announced positive preliminary results from its exploratory Phase 2 trial of setmelanotide in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). Setmelanotide therapy demonstrated potential therapeutic benefit with BMI and hyperphagia reductions in patients with PWS at Month 3 (n=8) and Month 6 (n=5); Safety and tolerability results have been consistent with setmelanotide's well-established clinical profile.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 1 Part D study in PWS
detailed_catalyst_text: A new Part D arm of the Phase 1 study of RM-718 was initiated to evaluate a weekly MC4R agonist in Prader-Willi syndrome. The Part D study is designed to enroll up to 20 patients in a 26-week open-label format, expanding clinical evaluation in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Company initiated Phase 1, Part D study to evaluate weekly MC4R agonist RM-718 in patients with PWS. Rhythm also announced that it has initiated a Part D arm in the Phase 1 trial of MC4R agonist RM-718 that will enroll up to 20 patients with PWS.

catalyst_text: Acceptance of sNDA with PDUFA date December 20, 2025.

Reported positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial evaluating setmelanotide for acquired hypothalamic obesity. Significant mean BMI reduction of 16.5% after 52 weeks, compared to a 3.3% increase in the placebo group (p<0.0001). This translates to a placebo-adjusted BMI reduction of 19.2% in adults and 20.2% in patients younger than 18 years old over the same period.
